company.name: Wispr Flow
company.oneLiner: Voice-to-text AI that turns natural speech into clear, polished writing in every app — 4x faster than typing.
company.description: Wispr Flow is a voice interface for writing. Hold a key, speak naturally, and Flow writes clean, formatted text in any app on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android — in 100+ languages, adapting to your style. It adds an AI notetaker for meetings, and sells to individuals (free and Pro) and to teams and enterprises with SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance.
company.stage: Venture-backed growth (2.5M organic monthly active users)

audience.primary: Knowledge workers, founders and developers who write all day
audience.buyer: Individuals first; team leads and IT for business plans
audience.user: Anyone who types for a living — email, Slack, docs and code prompts

jobsToBeDone: Prompt AI tools and code by voice
differentiators: Polished writing, not raw transcription — it cleans up as you speak
Works in every app and on every device
Personalised to your words and style

positioning.statement: For people who think faster than they type, Wispr Flow is the voice interface that turns natural speech into polished writing in any app — so you can speak at the speed you think.

pillars.name: 4x faster than typing
pillars.description: 220 wpm spoken versus 45 wpm typed — measured, not promised.

pillars.name: Sounds like you
pillars.description: Flow learns your vocabulary and style, and your voice stays private.

personality.summary: Wispr Flow feels like a beautifully printed book that talks. A literary serif with expressive italics, cream paper, deep green and a soft lavender button make a high-tech product feel human and a little poetic. It is witty ('You have a way with words. Now, two.'), confident about speed, and protective about privacy.
personality.archetype: The Poet-Engineer — eloquent on the surface, precise underneath.

traits.description: EB Garamond with italic emphasis ('just speak.', 'than typing') — literary, but headlines stay short.
Wordplay lands once per section: 'You have a way with words. Now, two.'
Speed is quantified (4x, 220 wpm) and shown with text flowing along curved paths — fluid, not frenetic.
Real people's photos and voices; product framed around how you work.

voice.summary: Short, crafted lines with a turn in them. Headlines are imperatives or crisp claims, often with an italic second half; supporting copy is plain and specific about speed, apps and privacy.

principles.name: Say it like speech
principles.description: Imperatives and contractions — the way you'd say it out loud.

principles.name: One turn of phrase
principles.description: A single, earned bit of wordplay per moment.
principles.do: You have a way with words. Now, two.
principles.dont: Unleash your inner wordsmith with the power of voice! 🎤

mechanics: Sentence case; headlines end with a period when they're statements.
Italic serif for the emphasized half of a headline.
Numerals for speed and scale ('4x', '220 wpm', '100+ languages').
Primary CTA names the platform: 'Get started on macOS'.

examples.offBrand: The AI dictation app that supercharges your productivity

examples.onBrand: Speak at the speed you think, in every app, on every device.
We didn't catch that. Hold Fn and try again.
45 wpm typing. 220 wpm speaking. Same thoughts, 4x sooner.

taglines: Speak at the speed you think.

visual.summary: Cream paper (#FFFFEB), soft black ink (#1A1A1A), deep forest green (#034F46) sections and a lavender (#F0D7FF) action button, set in EB Garamond with expressive italics over Figtree UI type. The signature visual is text flowing along curved paths, like speech becoming writing.

principles.name: Book typography, app product
principles.description: EB Garamond 400 for headlines (italics for emphasis) at very tight leading (0.85–0.95); Figtree for everything functional.

principles.name: Lavender acts
principles.description: The primary CTA is a lavender pill with dark text — soft, distinctive, never a default blue.

principles.name: Green for proof
principles.description: Deep green full-width bands hold the quantified claims (4x faster).

principles.name: Words in motion
principles.description: Spoken words travel along curved ribbons across the page — the brand's core metaphor.

visual.colorUsage: Cream dominates; ink for type and the customer band; forest green for proof sections; lavender reserved for CTAs; coral (#FF6C4C) and amber (#FFA946) as small accents in illustrations and tags.
visual.typography: EB Garamond for display (roman + italic contrast within a line); Figtree 500–600 for UI, eyebrows (+0.08em uppercase) and body.
visual.layout: Centered hero and section headers on a 1240px measure, full-bleed colored bands with large top radii (stacked cards), airy rhythm.
visual.imagery: Warm, motion-blurred lifestyle photography; product UI pills (the waveform 'listening' pill); monochrome customer logos on ink.
visual.iconography: Simple 1.5px icons; the waveform glyph is the recurring motif.
visual.shape: Pills for buttons and status; 24–32px radii on stacked full-width sections.
do: Pair a roman headline with an italic turn.
Use lavender only for the primary action.
Show words flowing along curves to express dictation.
dont: Don't use microphone clip-art or soundwave stock graphics.
Don't use a sans-serif for display headlines.
Don't use blue or purple gradients for 'AI'.

motion.summary: Fluid and literal: sentences travel along curved paths across the hero, the listening pill pulses with a waveform, and sections stack with GSAP-driven scroll. Lottie animations illustrate features. UI transitions are 200–350ms.

principles.name: Speech becomes text
principles.description: Motion visualises words flowing — continuous, never jittery.

principles.name: Calm stacking
principles.description: Sections slide up and stack like cards as you scroll.

motion.signature: Spoken sentences flowing along curved ribbons through the hero, ending in the waveform listening pill.

logo.clearspace: The height of the waveform mark on all sides.
logo.minSize: 16px for the mark; 20px tall for the wordmark.
misuse: Recolor outside ink, cream or white
Separate the waveform from the wordmark in lockups

copy.announcement: Wispr Flow Notetaker is now on Windows and Mac
